Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


*** This scenario removes Sudden Victory and Sudden Loss victory
rules. The game will always continue on to either the 31 December
1944 victory check, the fall of Berlin, or the end date of the
scenario.


Historical Overview
----------------------------------
Germany and its Axis Allies embark on a blitzkrieg campaign to
destroy the Soviet Union only to be stopped at the proverbial gates
of Moscow. Three and a half more years of bloody combat will follow
before the hammer & sickle flies over the Brandenburg Gate.

Scenario Overview
----------------------------------
Axis Player:
- Destroy the Red Army and decisively seize Moscow, Leningrad 
  and Rostov before the end of 1941.
- APs/Turn: 14
 
Soviet Player:
- Initially delay and disrupt Axis offensives, then conduct a strategic 
  counter-offensive to destroy the Axis armies and seize Berlin.
- APs/Turn: 20

Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
Early Winter 1942, the Red Army launches Operation MARS against
the German defenses in the Rzhev-Vyazma salient. The Soviet 3rd
Shock Army, supported by 3rd Air Army, begins the offensive by
attacking 3rd Panzer Army at Velikie Luki.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Soviet Player:
- Seize Velikie Luki and destroy Axis forces in order to open access
  along the Lovat River and enable further offensive operations.
- Concentrate to achieve decisive results against Wehrmacht units.
- Keep the initiative.
- APs/Turn: 5

Axis Player:
- Defend Velikie Luki and defeat Red Army penetration of the Lovat
  River in order to deny this vital area to the enemy.
- Seek opportunities to spoil Soviet attacks and impede their ability
  to concentrate by breaking up enemy formations and echelons with 
  your reinforcements.
- APs/Turn: 5

Author:  Miquel Ramirez - BletchleyGeek


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
As Operation Barbarossa begins, Army Group Center must envelop the
Soviet Armies in Belarus, capture the republic's capital of Minsk, and
push on to the Dnepr River.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Axis player:
- Use your infantry to break the Soviet front line on turn 1. Send
  your armor through the gaps you create, sweeping deep into the
  Soviet rear to capture Minsk and isolate as many units as possible.
- On turn 2, have the infantry clear the pockets while the armor
  continues to moves east.
- APs/Turn: 5

Soviet player:
- Delay the Axis advance as much as possible, and prevent them from
  capturing most of the objective cities.
- Try to break the pockets on turn one if the Axis leaves you an
  opening, or cut off armored spearheads and deny them the supply
  they will need for exploitation.
- APs/Turn: 10

Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


Historical Overview
------------------------------
Operations during July and August against Leningrad and Kiev have
ended and OKH has redeployed the mass of its armor to Army Group
Center. Its mission: capture the capital of the USSR, Moscow, and
bring down the Bolshevik 'house of cards'.

Scenario Overview
------------------------------
Axis Player:
- Break the Soviet front line with your infantry and exploit with
  your armored formations. Isolate, then destroy, as many units as
  possible in the early turns, then try to get in position for an
  assault on Moscow before the heavy rains arrive in October.
- You will have one more chance in November after the snow starts,
  but beware of Soviet counter attacks that may arrive with winter.
- APs/Turn: 25

Soviet Player:
- Try to save as many of your front-line units as possible while
  giving ground to the initial Axis offensive. Hold Moscow at all
  costs and counterattack once your reserves arrive as
  'General Winter' joins the fray in December.
- APs/Turn: 20

Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
November 1942: The Germans can finally claim 90% of Stalingrad. But
to get there the 6th Army has been completely committed, leaving
their flanks held only by Romanians and other allies. Stavka has been
planning a counterstroke for months and exploits this weakness - as
the snowfalls begin, the Red Army launches an offensive which will
change the course of the war.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Soviet Player:
- Break through the Axis allied forces to isolate and destroy the
  6th Army. If allowed to escape, they will severely hinder your
  goal of reclaiming key Ukrainian cities this winter. Further south
  you must keep up pressure to fix the Germans and exploit any
  withdrawals.
- APs/Turn: 15

Axis Player:
- The 6th Army must be preserved to check the Soviet winter
  offensives into the Ukraine, but political considerations (VPs) will
  not allow a bloodless withdrawal from Stalingrad. Reinforcements
  are en route, but alone cannot break out the 6th or prevent major
  Soviet gains.
- APs/Turn: 10

Authors:  Red Lancer and Randy Seger - rjs28023


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
November 1942: As the Red Army launches Uranus near Stalingrad,
it's Western and Kalinin Fronts launch Operation Mars to destroy the
Rzhev-Vyazma salient. Unlike the south, here the entire line is held
by German troops in good terrain. The fighting will be tough and
bloody, earning the offensive a sobriquet: 'the Rzhev Meatgrinder'.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Soviet Player:
- This is a tough enemy in good defensive positions; it will not be
  a campaign of dashing victories. Instead, find weak points in the
  German line and grind inexorably forward in a series of small gains
  that will ultimately secure your objectives.
- APs/Turn: 10

Axis Player:
- Most units under your command are capable of stopping the Soviets
  dead in their tracks, but you cannot be strong everywhere. The
  weather and terrain will make dislodging soviet gains difficult,
  but possible with concentrated effort. Hold your objectives for as
  long as practical, and then give ground grudgingly to avoid losing
  units.
- APs/Turn: 5

Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
Late June 1941, with Operation BARBAROSSA, the Axis begins a
blitzkrieg campaign to destroy the Soviet Union before the Russian
winter exhausts supplies and impedes their operations.  From East
Prussia, the Axis attacks northeast with Army Group North in order
to destroy the Red Army's Leningrad Front and guard the northern
flank of Army Group Center.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Axis Player:
- Attack northeast, oriented on Leningrad, and isolate and destroy
  Leningrad Front units in order to seize vital areas and deny
  Soviet access to the Baltic Sea. Use speed and audacity to envelop
  Soviet units more quickly than they can respond.
- APs/Turn: 4

Soviet Player:
- Under pressure, delay the Axis advance in order to preserve
  fighting strength and wear down the enemy. In order to fix Army
  Group Center in the south, maintain sufficient power and freedom
  of action north of the Daugava River to be an army in being.
- APs/Turn: 7

Author:  Randy Seger - rjs28023


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
The last German attempt to capture the remaining west bank of the
Volga in Stalingrad has failed. Meanwhile, on the flanks of the
German 6th Army, powerful forces under Generals Rokossovsky,
Eremenko, and Vatutin, are poised to cut off the German 6th Army.
Can the Soviet Army reverse the tide of Axis victories and ultimately
drive to Berlin?

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Soviet player:
- Drive rapidly to isolate the Axis around Stalingrad and, onward
  to the shores of the Sea of Azov to cut off Axis forces in the
  Caucasus.
- Build up your motorized forces so you can continue moving west
  after recapturing the initiative.
- APs/Turn: 35

Axis player:
- Withdraw before the Soviet juggernaut, consolidate your defenses,
  and hold on as long as possible. If you hold Germany in July 1945,
  you win!
- Powerful mechanized forces arrive in early 1943 that might allow
  you to make limited counteroffensives.
- APs/Turn: 25

IMPORTANT: This scenario is considered to be superseded by the new 
Campaign End Conditions game option.  We strongly recommend using 
that option along with the regular Stalingrad to Berlin Campaign 
instead of using this "No Early End" scenario, but this scenario 
remains available for players who prefer it.

Author:  Trey Marshall - Great_Ajax


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
As Barbarossa begins Army Group South attacks to seize the resource
rich Ukraine and a springboard to the Caucuses. The Soviet
Southwestern Front lies directly astride their planned advance and
mounts an unexpectedly fierce resistance, beginning a series of
bitter battles that will ultimately divert PG2 away from Moscow.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Axis Player:
- Attack to seize your initial objectives quickly and destroy the Red
  Army before they can form a coherent defense. Be prepared follow 
  up that success with a rapid thrust over the Dnepr to secure Rostov,
  Kharkov, and Kiev before the rains arrive.
- PG2 will arrive near Gomel in late August (T10).
- APs/Turn: 4

Soviet Player:
- At first you must contain the German advance while preserving your
  initial forces. Massed reinforcements which will allow a stiffer
  defense are en route, but will be useless if the Germans are
  allowed free rein before their arrival.
- APs/Turn: 7

Author:  Randy Seger - rjs28023


Historical Overview
---------------------------------
January, 1945: Six and a half million men of the Red Army stand ready 
to launch a final series of massive attacks meant to crush the Reich 
and end the war. The Wehrmacht is outnumbered, poorly positioned by 
direct orders from Hitler, and reeling from the Ardennes. With little
more than grim determination it prepares to meet the coming storm.

Scenario Overview
---------------------------------
Soviet Player:
- The ultimate goal is Berlin; you must maintain a continuous series
  of offensives aimed at reaching the city while other lines of
  attack pin and destroy the Axis forces. Do not let the Germans
  recover and consolidate or you will face a much stiffer defense.
- APs/Turn: 45

Axis Player:
- You must preserve Berlin. After weathering the opening attacks
  reform your lines and make a series of defensive stands to delay
  the battle for the capital as long as possible. If the rail links
  between Berlin and both Vienna and Prague are lost, your logistics
  will disintegrate once the Allies reach the Ruhr.
- APs/Turn: 25
